issue.title: apoc.text clean/split/replace/urlencode/urldecode/indexOf return different values from APOC 5.26.30
issue.note: Backend at the reproduction head is identical to shipped v1.5.1 cb0a574f per the delegated context. This corpus is reproduction evidence only; it authorizes no production change.

reference.route: public Cypher execution over the registered APOC plugin surface (the bundled plugin's compiled handlers), on both supported parser paths
reference.apoc: APOC Core 5.26.30, bundled jar sha256 4c60fdab264230d60745d31d55d6cb668e66061daba7c5fa6777ed457b49b798, RETURN apoc.version() = 5.26.30
reference.confirmed_rotation: NornicDB plugin handlers are installed from apoc.Initialize/GetInfo; none of the case owners is an engine built-in, so no built-in shortcut can answer these calls
reference.fresh_reference: fresh-parent-reference.json - every apoc.text expectation below is that run's result for the same query; the six apoc.util names are recorded there as absent from APOC (missing_function), so their advertised NornicDB expectation is unchanged

retest_b098f7e70.content: Retested on release head b098f7e70 (#1683); NOT FIXED; same reproduction as 31208b17f.

retest_31208b17f.content: Verification on 31208b17f (#1682); all six recorded differences reproduce: clean, split, replace, urlencode, urldecode, indexOf.

capitalize_decapitalize_nulls.content: capitalize('') fails in APOC (Strings.java substring on empty); decapitalize(null) returns null in APOC, while both parser paths reject null for func(string)string. capitalize('') expectation to be decided against APOC.

label_normalize_moved.content: apoc.label.normalize moved to NOR-290; out of this issue.

base64_url_placeholders.content: apoc.text base64 and apoc.util Base64/URL registrations are identity/two-character placeholders; registrations advertise real Base64 and full percent-encoding.

converter_runtime_values.content: Runtime-confirmed converter values: upperCamelCase('ßeta world')=SSetaWorld, upperCamelCase('ǳungla world')=ǱunglaWorld, camelCase('𐐨abc world')=𐐀abcWorld, punctuation removed for both converters, camelCase('hello foo.bar')=helloFooBar.

converter_source_values.content: Source-derived converter values (Strings.java 559-569, 576-577): camelCase removes punctuation; upperCamelCase uppercases the first UTF-16 unit.

out_of_scope: production fixes, edits to other worktrees, commits, pushes, PRs, external writes, SSH or Docker

Original issue row; APOC replaces every regex match, NornicDB replaces the literal old string.
A literal-safe pattern repeats; both owners agree today, which the observed assertion records.
No match leaves the text unchanged.
Java Matcher replacement expands $1; the Go owner would need equivalent replacement semantics.

The fresh APOC reference fails this call as a function error instead of returning a value. The exported NornicDB owner returns 'abc' unchanged and cannot signal an error, so parity needs an error path; error text identity is not asserted.
Original issue row; APOC percent-encodes reserved and non-ASCII characters.

Java URLEncoder form-encodes space as '+' and the fresh APOC reference returns hello+world; apoc/apoc.go:425 advertises hello%20world for the same call, so the registration example must be corrected by the separately authorized fix.
UTF-8 percent-encoding of a BMP non-ASCII character.
Original issue row; %2B decodes to a literal plus.
apoc/apoc.go:426 advertises this exact call, and Java URLDecoder agrees.
Java URLDecoder decodes '+' as space, as apoc/apoc.go:426's own example requires.

The fresh APOC reference fails this call as a function error on the malformed percent escape. The exported NornicDB owner returns '%zz' unchanged and cannot signal an error, so parity needs an error path; error text identity is not asserted.
Original issue row; APOC reports a UTF-16 code-unit index, NornicDB a UTF-8 byte offset.
apoc/apoc.go:429 advertises this exact call.
A BMP character is one UTF-16 code unit and two UTF-8 bytes.
U+10428 is one supplementary code point, two UTF-16 code units and four UTF-8 bytes. The fresh APOC reference returns 2, the UTF-16 code-unit index of 'abc'; the byte-offset owner returns 4.
Java String.indexOf returns -1 and the fresh APOC reference run confirms -1 for a missing substring; the original matrix only said 'missing result'.

The fresh APOC reference fails apoc.text.capitalize('') as a function error while NornicDB returns ''. Asserted through public execution on both parser paths only, because the exported Go owner cannot return an error.
The fresh APOC reference returns null (StringUtils.uncapitalize accepts null); both NornicDB parser paths reject null for a func(string)string.

NornicDB advertises neither a route nor a query-form contract for '+' in this extension. Path-style decoding keeps '+' and form-style decoding maps it to space.
Runtime-confirmed APOC 5.26.30 value; the first UTF-16 unit uppercases with string expansion.
Runtime-confirmed APOC 5.26.30 value; uppercase of ǳ is Ǳ (not titlecase ǲ).
Runtime-confirmed APOC 5.26.30 value; lowercasing the first UTF-16 unit is a no-op on a lone high surrogate, so the uppercase form remains.

The fresh APOC reference returns ßetaWorld: camelCase lowercases the whole first code point, so ß stays ß instead of the derived 'sSetaWorld'.
The fresh APOC reference returns ǳunglaWorld: lowercasing Ǳ yields ǳ.
The fresh APOC reference returns 𐐀abcWorld: upperCamelCase uppercases the first code point (U+10428 -> U+10400) instead of the derived lone-surrogate no-op.
